messages.author: 09570c3cdd137595
messages.subject: Error with false-positive modeling in occuFP: "Error in pvec * (1 - bvec) : non-conformable arrays"
parts:
Hi all,

My apologies for what may be a simple answer to this question. I have spent many hours trying to find a solution, to no avail.

I am currently analyzing a dataset of jaguar occupancy across 1442 sites (it's for all of Central America, hence the number of sites). We have a maximum of 6 occasions per site.

I have been able to run standard single-season models in unmarked just fine with these data, and yet when I use unmarkedFrameOccuFP and occuFP I get the error message "Error in pvec * (1 - bvec) : non-conformable arrays." The error message leads me to believe that the data going into unmarkedFrameOccuFP are not of the correct dimension, though I have done many checks to ensure that they are--- plus, the models run in occu just fine. I have cells with missing data, as we were not able to collect 6 surveys in all sites. There are also sites with zero surveys. Perhaps this is a problem for occuFP?

Or maybe I am using incorrect syntax, specifically in the "type" argument, as that appears to be the only difference in preparing data for occu and occuFP.

I have provided my code below. Crossing my fingers and hoping that someone is able to help.

My thanks,
Lisanne Petracca


#set working directory
setwd("I:/Jaguar_Corridor_Single_Occupancy_Analysis/Occupancy")

#import 32 site covariates for 1442 sites
as.data.frame(site_cov<-read.csv("SiteCovariates.csv", header=T, row.names=1))

#import detection history--- composed of 0s, 1s, and 2s--- 2s are certain detections, 1s uncertain
as.data.frame(detect<-read.csv("Jaguar_Max6.csv", header=T, row.names=1))

#Convert dashes to NA for Unmarked
detect[detect=="-"] <-NA 
detect<-apply(detect, 2, function(x){as.numeric(as.character(x))})

#import three detection covariates
as.data.frame(effort<-read.csv("Effort_Max6.csv", header=T, row.names=1))
effort[effort=="-"]<-NA 
effort<-apply(effort, 2, function(x){as.numeric(as.character(x))}) 

as.data.frame(year<-read.csv("Year_Max6.csv", header=T, row.names=1))
year[year=="-"]<-NA 
year<-apply(year, 2, function(x){as.factor(as.character(x))}) 

as.data.frame(corridor<-read.csv("Corridor_Max6.csv", header=T, row.names=1))
corridor[corridor=="-"]<-NA 
corridor<-apply(corridor, 2, function(x){as.factor(as.character(x))})

#declare that all six occasions are of type III (certain and uncertain detections, accounting for false positives)
type <- as.vector(c(0, 0, 6))

#build OccuFP data frame
Jagmodel<-unmarkedFrameOccuFP(y=detect, siteCovs=site_cov, obsCovs=list(effort=effort, year=year, corridor=corridor), type=type) 

#build first model
fm.null <- occuFP(detformula = ~ 1, FPformula = ~ 1, Bformula = ~ 1, stateformula = ~ 1, data = Jagmodel)

parts:
Hi Folks,

I have started to use occuFP a bit to get familiar with how it works, and doesn't. I thought I would share a couple of things that i have found:
  1. you cannot, currently, do model selection with these models
  2. the fitting function does not like NA's in the encounter histories (works fine if those sites are removed - I think this was the issue in the questions below) 
I'm not so familiar with the unmarked code base, but will try and work on these fixes when I get the opportunity!

Chris
